pages.text: `x² + 6x` is an `x` by `x` square with a strip 6 wide beside it. Cut the strip in half and swing one half round to the bottom, so both sides grow by 3. The pieces nearly make a square with sides `x + 3`, missing a 3 by 3 corner, so `x² + 6x` is `(x + 3)² − 9`.

pages.task: Cut the strip of `x² + 8x` in half and swing one half round. What is the missing corner?
pages.why: Half of 8 is 4, so each side grows by 4 and the corner is 4 by 4, which is 16. So `x² + 8x` is `(x + 4)² − 16`, and at `x = 1` both give 9.

pages.text: `(x + 3)²` is never below zero, and it is zero at `x = −3`, so `(x + 3)² − 7` is lowest there, at −7. That bottom of the U, `(−3, −7)`, is its [[turning point]], and since points the same distance either side of −3 give the same square, the curve is a mirror image about the line `x = −3`, its [[line of symmetry]]. Slide `b` and the turning point moves to `x = −b ÷ 2`, dropping by the corner.

pages.task: Solving `x² + 4x + 1 = 0`, the first line is `x² + 4x = −1`. What is the next line?
pages.why: Add the corner, 4, to both sides, so the left becomes `(x + 2)²` and the right `−1 + 4 = 3`. Then `x + 2` is `√3` or `−√3`, and `x` is about −0.27 or −3.73.

pages.task: Which is `2x² + 12x + 5` with its square completed?
pages.why: Take the 2 out of the first two terms, so `2(x² + 6x) + 5`. Then `x² + 6x` is `(x + 3)² − 9`, and the 9 comes off twice, `2 × 9 = 18`. So it is `2(x + 3)² − 13`, and at `x = 1` both give 19.

pages.task: Which is `−x² + 6x − 4` with its square completed?
pages.why: Take the minus out first, so `−(x² − 6x) − 4`. Half of −6 is −3, so `x² − 6x` is `(x − 3)² − 9`, and the minus in front turns −9 into +9: `−(x − 3)² + 9 − 4`, which is `−(x − 3)² + 5`. Its highest point is `(3, 5)`, and at `x = 1` both give 1.
